changelog.body:
**New since 1.12.10** (same signing key: installs over 1.12.8–1.12.10, no uninstall needed; reboot after updating).

- New option **"Dim the monitor with the light sensor"** (Monitor section, off by default). Android can't change an external monitor's backlight (no DDC/CI access on stock kernels, and most monitors don't expose brightness over USB), so the module darkens the picture in software: a transparent black layer on the monitor that follows the phone's ambient light sensor with a smooth fade. Full picture from about 200 lux, only a little dimming under normal indoor light, most of it in a really dark room.
- Slider **"Maximum dimming in the dark"** (10–90%, default 50%).
- Tip: set the monitor's own brightness to a medium-low level and let the module handle the rest. The diagnostic report shows the current lux and dimming (`auto-dim:` line).

New since 1.12.8 (same signing key: installs over 1.12.8, no uninstall needed; reboot after updating).

    Main switch at the top of the module's settings ("Module enabled"). Off: the monitor goes back to mirroring, the phone screen and the dock go back to normal, and every hook lets HyperOS behave as stock, without a reboot and without touching LSPosed. Desktop mode is fully stock again after reconnecting the monitor or rebooting. The Monitor tile and the diagnostics line show when the module is off.
    New option "Don't open HyperOS's own desktop on the monitor" (Dock section, off by default). Keeps the stock Xiaomi desktop (SecondaryDisplayLauncher) off the monitor and closes it if it is already open. Try it if the phone's gestures stop working after you change the monitor's density or scale. The dock and your apps are not affected.
    Simplified Chinese translation.

Thanks to @oldbkroll, whose fork had the first version of these three ideas.

⚠️ New package name: uninstall the old version. The module's package is now io.github.the_marox.hyperdesktop (it was io.maurizio.hyperdesktop), as required by the official LSPosed module repository. Android treats it as a different app, so it won't replace the old one:

    Unplug the monitor and uninstall the old HyperDesktop Unlock.
    Install this APK.
    LSPosed → Modules → enable HyperDesktop Unlock with scope System Framework, System UI, Settings, then reboot.

The module's settings start from the defaults. If the old version is still installed, the new settings app shows a warning with a button to uninstall it.

No functional changes since 1.12.7.

readme:
# HyperDesktop Unlock

Turns an external USB-C monitor into a **separate desktop display** (not a mirror) on Xiaomi phones running **HyperOS 4 (Android 17)**, where Xiaomi ships Android's connected-display / desktop code but keeps it disabled.

## Features
- Brings back the hidden **Computer** (Desktop) button in the "Connect to external display" dialog
- The monitor gets its own status bar and mouse cursor; apps opened there stay there
- Neutralises Xiaomi's mirroring enforcer (`SecondaryDisplayPolicy`)
- Starts [SmartDock](https://github.com/axel358/smartdock) (or Taskbar) on the monitor and turns off the phone screen
- Optional **touchpad mode**: the phone controls the monitor's pointer (tap, two-finger scroll and right click, pinch to zoom, edge swipe for Back), with the on-screen keyboard on the phone
- Desktop keyboard shortcuts: Alt+Tab with preview bar, monitor screenshots, Win+Shift+Arrow to move apps between displays, Alt+F4, Win+D, Win+P…
- Quick Settings tiles (Computer ↔ Mirroring, Touchpad), monitor density/resolution/refresh settings, diagnostic report

## Requirements
- Xiaomi phone with DisplayPort Alt Mode over USB-C (tested: Xiaomi 15, Xiaomi 14)
- HyperOS 4 / Android 17
- Scope: **System Framework**, **System UI**, **Settings**, then reboot

## Limits
No resizable windows or title bars: HyperOS doesn't expose AOSP's desktop windowing, so apps run full screen on the monitor.

Full documentation, troubleshooting and source code: https://github.com/the-marox/HyperDesktopUnlock
readmeZh:
# 超级桌面解锁

在运行 **HyperOS 4 (Android 17)** 的小米手机上将外部 USB-C 显示器变成 **独立的桌面显示器**（不是镜子），其中小米提供 Android 的连接显示器/桌面代码，但保持禁用状态。

## 特点
- 在“连接到外部显示器”对话框中恢复隐藏的**计算机**（桌面）按钮
- 显示器有自己的状态栏和鼠标光标；在那里打开的应用程序停留在那里
- 中和小米的镜像执行器（`SecondaryDisplayPolicy`）
- 在显示器上启动 [SmartDock](https://github.com/axel358/smartdock)（或任务栏）并关闭手机屏幕
- 可选**触摸板模式**：手机使用手机上的屏幕键盘控制显示器的指针（点击、两指滚动和右键单击、捏合缩放、边缘滑动返回）
- 桌面键盘快捷键：Alt+Tab 带预览栏、显示器屏幕截图、Win+Shift+箭头在显示器之间移动应用程序、Alt+F4、Win+D、Win+P...
- 快速设置图块（计算机↔镜像、触摸板）、显示器密度/分辨率/刷新设置、诊断报告

## 要求
- 通过 USB-C 配备 DisplayPort Alt 模式的小米手机（测试：小米 15、小米 14）
- HyperOS 4 / Android 17
- 范围：**系统框架**、**系统 UI**、**设置**，然后重新启动

## 限制
没有可调整大小的窗口或标题栏：HyperOS 不会公开 AOSP 的桌面窗口，因此应用程序在显示器上全屏运行。

完整文档、故障排除和源代码：https://github.com/the-marox/HyperDesktopUnlock
